tasks.return: Write down the route and latest return time.
tasks.junctions: Mark junctions as they will look on the way back.
tasks.paper: Pack a paper map, pencil and compass.
tasks.water: Check the refill point and carry water for the return.

questions.prompt: Two tracks look alike on the return from Hatta. What would help you recognize your junction?
choices: The total length of the walk
A sketch of the junction facing home
The height of the starting point
questions.heading: Draw the return route first

questions.prompt: You have a GPS fix and little battery left. What belongs on your paper route card?
choices: Coordinates, accuracy, time and a nearby landmark
Estimated distance walked and phone battery level
The town name and the map zoom level
questions.heading: Record a fix everyone can read

questions.prompt: Your planned turnaround time arrives while the viewpoint is still ahead. Which entry governs your decision?
choices: The original estimate of the trail length
The distance from the viewpoint
The return time and supply threshold you set before leaving
questions.heading: Use a turnaround rule

tasks.count: Measure the drinking water already on hand.
tasks.primary: Confirm a working drinking-water point and access.
tasks.backup: Write down a second reachable refill point.
tasks.containers: Separate clean drinking containers from collection vessels.

questions.prompt: Your offline map shows a well. What can you conclude from the symbol alone?
choices: The well is open to the public
The water is ready to drink
A well was mapped at that location
questions.heading: Read a water symbol correctly

questions.prompt: Your planned refill is marked on an old map. What makes the route more dependable?
choices: Checking access and confirming a second reachable supply
Saving the same pin on a second screen
Writing down the distance to the pin alone
questions.heading: Make a two-source route

questions.prompt: You have six sealed 1.5 litre bottles. What amount do you enter as your starting stock?
choices: 6 litres
9 litres
15 litres
questions.heading: Start with water you can account for

tasks.torch: Put a working torch by the door and shoes near each bed.
tasks.stock: Count water, ready-to-eat meals and charged lights.
tasks.cool: Identify a cooler place the household can reach.
tasks.handover: Write down who holds the keys and the next check-in time.

questions.prompt: The power cuts out in your apartment. Which time should go in your household log first?
choices: When the freezer was last stocked
When power failed
When the household usually eats dinner
questions.heading: Mark the time and light the route

questions.prompt: Another person takes over the household watch. Which note helps them act?
choices: The outage start time without the next check-in
A supply list without names or locations
Who has keys and supplies, and when to check in next
questions.heading: Plan the handover

questions.prompt: Your supply ledger started at 18 litres. After using 7 litres, what goes in the remaining-stock column?
choices: 11 litres
7 litres
18 litres
questions.heading: Work a day on paper
